title: Finite generic fibers become a finite morphism near the generic points
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] which is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $Y$ be Noetherian (locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact). Suppose the set-theoretic fiber $f^{-1}(\{\eta\})$ is finite for every generic point $\eta$ of every irreducible component of $Y$. Then there exists a dense open subscheme $V\subseteq Y$ containing all these generic points such that $f^{-1}(V)\to V$ is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism].
